birth_time_sensitivity/approximate_hour.method: Classifications (every non-numeric value each resampled path prints: the sign of every longitude, angle, cusp and Lot; house placements of planets and Lots; motion direction; sect and its near-horizon band; the Lot formula basis; the void-of-course flag only; the twelfth-part of every point the chart lists) are recomputed at the listed sampled instants of the stated civil hour [H:00,H+1:00) in the named fold: a quarter-hour grid plus the seconds either side of any UTC-offset change inside the hour, located by a one-minute UTC scan refined to the second. same_at_all_samples means only that those sampled instants agree; it is not proof that the classification holds between them, and no invariant is applied to exclude a change and reversal between adjacent samples. Adjacent samples that differ are bisected to at most 15 s; each bracket holds at least one change, not necessarily one. A twelfth-part's or an extended Lot's own change is not bisected: its classifications are those seen at the samples and at the midpoints other changes needed. Inside the polar circle the Ascendant can reverse between samples, so every path read off it is at most partially evaluated. Numeric values are sampled envelopes, not states. Every sample fails closed when its calculation did not use the Swiss files.

birth_time_sensitivity/date_only.method: Classifications of bodies and nodes (every non-numeric value they print: sign, motion direction, reason codes) and of the planets' twelfth-parts are recomputed at the listed sampled instants of the local civil day, every instant the zone labels with the date (one or more UTC stretches): every existing hourly clock label on both folds, the first and last second of each stretch, and the seconds either side of every UTC-offset change that fall on the date, located by a one-minute UTC scan refined to the second. same_at_all_samples means only that those sampled instants agree; it is not proof that the classification holds between them, and no invariant is applied to exclude a change and reversal between adjacent samples. A Moon sign transition between the last sample of one stretch and the first of the next is marked as across another date: part of the time between them is labelled with another date. Numeric values are sampled envelopes, not states. Every sample fails closed when its calculation did not use the Swiss files.

classical_classifications.above_horizon_rule: Above the earth means the planet centre's geocentric true altitude is above 0 deg, the rule this product uses for the Sun's sect. The sources say only 'above/under the earth' and do not choose between the horizon and the house division.
classical_classifications.joy_houses: A joy is met when the planet's house in the chart's selected house division is the named place.
classical_classifications.mercury_sect: Mercury's sect follows Ptolemy I.7 (morning star diurnal, evening star nocturnal), judged by ecliptic longitude east or west of the Sun; al-Bīrūnī gives no computable rule and Valens I.1 none.
classical_classifications.rule: Each classification is the named source's own; where sources differ each gets its own field. Nothing is summed or scored. The places' meanings are not part of the chart output.

decennials.statement: Each planet in turn rules 129 months of 30 days (10 years 9 months of the 360-day year), starting from the profile's planet and following the natal zodiacal order of the seven planets by longitude; after the seventh the first rules again. Inside each level-1 period the lord itself comes first, then the others in the same natal order, each for its minor years as months (the seven minor years total 129, so level 2 fills level 1 exactly). Boundaries are the birth JD(UT) plus the accumulated days. Levels 1 and 2 only. The Chaldean order is never used.
decennials.table_order_note: The VI.6a table lists the sub-periods in the Chaldean order (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon from each lord); Valens's own worked example (VI.6) runs them in the natal zodiacal order, and VI.7 rejects the Chaldean order for finding the lord. The product follows the example and VI.7.

dignities/peregrine_lilly_1647_p112_v1.rule: A planet is peregrine when, at its degree, it holds none of the five essential dignities: whole-sign domicile or exaltation, the triplicity of the chart's sect ruler only (Lilly p.102), a term in Lilly's p.104 table, or a face (the Chaldean order, which Lilly's p.104 face column prints). Peregrine and detriment or fall can hold together. Reception does not remove peregrination: Bonatti lists the two as separate impediments, and Māshāʾallāh writes 'peregrinus, non receptus'. Only Lilly states that the sect ruler alone counts; Bonatti and Gadbury do not say.

dodecatemoria.default_basis: The only text read in its own words that states the rule and works an example is Firmicus II.13, and it multiplies by 12 from the start of the sign; the 2 deg 30 min division of Manilius and Ptolemy gives the same sign. The 13-fold rule is attested by the examples of Paulus and Olympiodorus as reported by Greenbaum and Jones; both are offered.
dodecatemoria.documentary_evidence: P.Berl. 9825 (horoscope of 319 CE) gives the twelfth-part signs only. Greenbaum and Jones 2017 para. 188: the Moon, Saturn, Jupiter (at its corrected position), Mars and Venus match the 13-fold formula; Mercury, both nodes and the prenatal full Moon do not, and match the 12-fold formula, which also fits Saturn, Jupiter and Mars. So only the Moon and Venus favour the 13-fold rule against the 12-fold one, and three planets fit both. They leave two explanations open: the 13-fold rule with the minutes neglected, or the 12-fold rule miscalculated for the Moon and Venus.
dodecatemoria.lord_rule: The lord listed is the domicile lord of the twelfth-part's sign in the traditional seven-planet scheme (the product's domicile table). Later steps that look at which planets occupy or aspect that sign are not computed; this product lists positions and lords only.
dodecatemoria.not_computed: Manilius's further division of each part among the five planets; the midheaven (no witness read); judgements of which planets occupy or aspect the twelfth-part.

profiles.thirteenfold_from_sign_start_v1: Multiply the degrees inside the sign by 13 and count on from the start of the same sign; the same as multiplying by 12 and counting on from the point's own degree. The product multiplies the full position, minutes included; the worked examples of Paulus and Olympiodorus use whole degrees, and Greenbaum and Jones infer that P.Berl. 9825 multiplied the whole degrees and disregarded the minutes.
profiles.twelvefold_from_sign_start_v1: Multiply the degrees and minutes inside the sign by 12 and count the product on from the start of the same sign, 30 to each sign. The product's default. At sign level this equals the division of each sign into twelve parts of 2 deg 30 min given to the sign itself and the following signs in order.

dodecatemoria.sect_band: When the Sun is in the near-horizon band and the Lots show both formulas, each Lot row says whether the other sect's formula gives another twelfth-part sign (sign_differs_under_other_sect, comparison_sign), as the zodiacal-releasing rows do; the listed value follows the product's sect rule.

eclipses/prenatal_selection.classical_use: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos II.4-II.8 (Robbins) uses eclipses chiefly for regions, cities and public affairs: II.4 calls the conjunctions of the Sun and Moon at eclipse 'the first and most potent cause' of such events; II.8 calls the positions in which a luminary of a nativity holds the degree of an eclipse (one after the birth) or the opposite degree 'most dangerous and hardest to avoid'; II.6 times the effect by the hours the obscuration lasts. Treating the last eclipse before birth as a point of the nativity is a twentieth-century practice (Jansky 1977, Lineman 1984 and 1992, Brady 1992, Graves 2004; secondary only). No source read says whether a penumbral lunar eclipse counts
eclipses/prenatal_selection.definition: the last solar and lunar eclipse whose Swiss maximum is before birth, as astronomical events. The lunar one includes penumbral eclipses; the last eclipse in which the Moon enters the umbra (partial or total) is listed beside it. The eclipse degree is the Sun's longitude at a solar eclipse and the Moon's at a lunar one, at the maximum. An eclipse whose first contact is at or before birth and whose maximum is after it is listed as under way
eclipses/prenatal_selection.penumbral_note: In a penumbral lunar eclipse the Moon passes only through the Earth's outer, partial shadow (the penumbra) and never reaches the dark core (the umbra). Espenak (eclipsewise.com, Visual Appearance of Lunar Eclipses): a penumbral magnitude above about 0.6 is needed before skilled observers can detect faint shading, the early and late stages are invisible, and it becomes readily apparent only within about 0.05 magnitude of a partial eclipse. For including it: it is an eclipse in the astronomical catalogues (NASA's lunar catalogue lists it, type N) and in Swiss Ephemeris's default search. For excluding it: Ptolemy's eclipses are visible obscurations (II.5: those 'in which the eclipse, since it took place above the earth, was visible'; II.6 times their effects by how many hours 'the obscuration' lasts). No astrological source read states a rule for penumbral eclipses; both are listed and none is chosen

monthly_profection.statement: Month k (k = 1-12) of year of life N+1 is the annual profection sign moved k-1 signs on in zodiacal order, so the first month is the year's own sign and the count starts again at every solar return; the lord of the month is that sign's seven-planet domicile lord. By default month k begins when the Sun has moved 30(k-1) degrees past its natal longitude, so the first month begins at the return and the twelfth ends at the next one; the named alternative cuts the return year into twelve equal parts. Whole signs only; the sect is not read. No degree, no topic of the place and no verdict is emitted.

motion_states.boundary_rule: exact rational comparison of |speed| in arcseconds a day with the printed mean; equal when the difference is less than half the last printed unit; a turn exactly Lilly's days ahead, or at the instant itself, counts as stationary; after a turn, an instant exactly Lilly's days after it still counts
motion_states.daily_motion_basis: The texts' daily motion is the difference of two noon positions; the product uses the instantaneous speed. Measured 1950-2050 (Swiss Ephemeris, geocentric): against the next 24 hours the Moon's swift/slow differs on 3.6% of instants (Mercury 1.4%, Saturn 0.5%, Mars 0.1%); against the 24 hours centred on the instant, 0.025% (Mercury 0.005%).
motion_states.definition: Course: the absolute geocentric longitude speed (Swiss Ephemeris analytic speed at the instant) against the mean daily motion; more is swift, less is slow (Lilly p.168), equal only within half the last place the source printed. A retrograde planet is compared by the degrees it goes back a day (Lilly p.178 calls a retrograde Saturn of 2 minutes a day slow). Stations: every sign change of the geocentric speed within 15 days before or after the chart instant, by root-finding; a planet is stationary when a turn falls within Lilly's days after the instant, or the instant within Lilly's days after a turn. Oriental or occidental of the Sun: the side of the Sun from solar_phase, west of the Sun (rising before it) oriental (Lilly p.114); the Moon oriental from opposition to conjunction; the Sun has none. Listed: the Sun, the Moon and the five planets.
doctrine: Lilly 1647 p.115: swift in motion, Saturn, Jupiter and Mars oriental, Venus and Mercury occidental, the Moon increasing or occidental are accidental fortitudes; slow in motion, Saturn, Jupiter and Mars occidental, Venus and Mercury oriental, the Moon decreasing in light are debilities

Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos I.24 (Robbins pp.115-117): planets oriental and adding to their motion are most powerful; occidental and diminishing in speed, weaker
al-Biruni, Book of Instruction §486: the influence is greatest when oriental and weak when occidental
Vettius Valens, Anthologies IV.14: passing the first station into retrograde delays what is expected; the second station removes the delay

Most treat a diurnal or nocturnal birth as a given category, or describe planetary conditions as above or below the earth; the closest to a solar day/night criterion are Valens III.11 (Pingree; = III.14 Kroll/Riley, '14K;11P'; the Moon 'above the earth' read as until it sets) and Lilly 1647 p.42 (checking the chart time by the Sun's house). solar_phase.boundary_rule: membership by exact rational comparison of the float |difference| with the limit in whole arcseconds; each limit inclusive or exclusive as worded
solar_phase.decision_basis_argument: Inference by this product, not a statement found in a source: al-Biruni (Book of Instruction §483) says a Venus whose north latitude exceeds 7 degrees at the conjunction is to be called neither samim nor combust but 'accompanying the Sun', and that at her greatest north latitude she remains visible; Abu Ma'shar (Great Introduction VII.2, Latin of Hermann of Carinthia) says Venus can be seen 'ex eodem cum Sole gradu' because of her latitude and is then not to be called burnt but appearing. Had these authors measured the true distance on the sky, such a Venus would already be 7-8 degrees from the Sun, outside 16 minutes and outside 6 degrees, and no exception would be needed; the exception is needed because the distance they read is in degrees of the zodiac (longitude), on which this Venus stands in the Sun's own degree.
solar_phase.default_basis: Lilly p.113 was read in the 1647 text, gives a limit for every band, and halves the Sun's orb of 17 degrees (p.107) that the product's default aspect orbs already use. Lilly himself writes 12 degrees and 16 minutes in aphorism 26 (p.300 as cited by Houlding; no page number in the transcription read); that disagreement is disclosed, not resolved.
solar_phase.definition: The signed difference of ecliptic longitude, body minus Sun, in (-180, 180]; the band is read from |difference| against the profile's limits for the side the body is on (negative: west of the Sun, rising before it, the morning side). The true angular separation and the ecliptic latitude are listed and decide nothing, except the optional solar-disc cazimi (separation at most the Sun's apparent semidiameter at that instant), which changes only the cazimi band. Listed: the Moon and the five planets. All three profiles are computed; the selected one fills rows[].
doctrine: Lilly 1647 p.111: 'the combustion of any Planet is the greatest misfortune that can be'
Lilly 1647 p.113: when the Sun applies to the planet it is more afflicted than when the Sun separates from it; 'all Authors doe hold a Planet in Cazimi to be fortified thereby'
Lilly aphorism 26: under the beams within 12 degrees it 'hath no fortitude'; within 16 minutes in Cazimi it is 'wonderous strong'
al-Biruni §481: under the rays 'they remain like prisoners in confinement'; §486: the influence 'is at its minimum in combustion'
Abu Ma'shar, Great Introduction VII.2 (Latin): the Sun burns, weakens and corrupts every star joined to it except one in zamim
Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos III.10 (Robbins p.285): no planet under the rays of the Sun is admitted to destroy or to aid
solar_phase.interval_rule: for a non-exact birth time, every band each profile puts each body in over the stated hour or civil day, from the roots of every band edge; the least and greatest difference over it sampled every half hour and at the ends
solar_phase.not_applied: Bonatti and al-Qabisi require the latitude as well as the longitude within 16 minutes for cazimi (al-Qabisi Introduction III, John of Seville's Latin translation read; Bonatti via Dykes 2007 p.211, secondary); the optional solar-disc reading comes close but is not their rule. Abu Ma'shar's own limits (combust 6 degrees, Mars 10; under the rays east 15, Mars 18) are not offered as a profile. Visibility by place and atmosphere (Swiss heliacal functions) is not computed.

profiles.biruni_wright_v1: al-Biruni §481-484: samim under 16 minutes (exclusive); combust to 6 degrees, to 7 degrees for Mercury and Venus in direct motion (§482); the Moon combust under 7 degrees and under the rays to 12 degrees (§484); under the rays rising in the east (morning side) to 12 Venus and Mercury, 15 Saturn and Jupiter, 16 Mars, setting in the west (evening side) from 16 Saturn and Jupiter, 18 Mars; Mercury and Venus take 12 on both sides, since §482 says only that their west 'resembles' the superior planets'; Venus north of 7 degrees latitude in the samim or combust band is 'accompanying the Sun' (§483).
profiles.hellenistic_15_v1: One band, under the beams within 15 degrees on either side; no cazimi or combust band (Porphyry, Antiochus as reported by Brennan 2017).
profiles.lilly_1647_p113_v1: Lilly 1647 p.113: cazimi within 17 minutes, combust within 8 deg 30 min, under the Sun-beams until 17 degrees; every limit inclusive; the same numbers for every body and side. The default.

solar_phase.same_sign_rule: Lilly p.113-114: combustion only by bodily conjunction in one sign, not by aspect. No other source read has the rule and Lilly's aphorism 26 puts a planet under the beams 'in what Signe it will'; the product reports same_sign_as_sun and does not apply the rule. In the sidereal zodiac only this flag can differ; the distance and the band cannot.
solar_phase.seven_day_rule: For the five planets, every crossing of the profile's under-the-beams limit within 7 days before or after the chart instant, emerging or sinking; stations not searched; the Moon not searched. The 7-day rule is reported from Porphyry, Introduction ch.30 and Rhetorius (Holden 2009 pp.24, 134) via a secondary page; the original was not read.

void_of_course.sign_condition: The Moon not perfecting an aspect before leaving its sign: Māshāʾallāh, On Reception ch.1 (Dykes 2008 p.443; ch.7, p.467, not checked) gives a general sign-boundary rule for planets, and applying it to the Moon and the void course is this site's application; Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647 p.112 'Voyd of course' (bounded by the sign; the page does not mention moieties). Sahl's definition in the Latin Quadripartitum collection (Venice 1519) is that the Moon joins no planet and none joins it; it names neither the sign boundary nor an orb. An earlier explicit statement is attributed to Abū Maʿshar, Abbreviation III.21-22 (not consulted).

year_boundary.statement: Year N+1 of life is [SR_N, SR_N+1): from the N-th solar return to the next, SR_0 being the birth instant. A non-whole year y = k + f is SR_k + f (SR_k+1 - SR_k), linear inside its own return year (product convention). The search window is centred on birth + N mean years (365.24219 days tropical, 365.256363 days sidereal); that number places the search and enters no result.

zodiacal_releasing.statement: Released from the signs of the Lot of Fortune and the Lot of Spirit (Daimon), both listed. A sign's period is its number from the period table: years at level 1, months (a twelfth of the year model) at level 2. Level-2 periods start in the parent's sign, follow zodiacal order and are cut where the parent ends (nominal length kept beside the effective one). When a circle of twelve signs (211 units) is complete before the parent ends, the next period starts at the sign opposite that circle's start (loosing of the bond), never the trine. Boundaries are the birth JD(UT) plus the accumulated days of the year model. Places are counted from the sign of Fortune for both lots, with the count from the starting lot beside it.

zr_year_360_days_v1.basis: Valens IV.9 'The Universal Year' (Kroll p.169): the universal year has 365 1/4 days, the year of the distribution 360; IV.4: the 17 years 7 months are allotted 'not counting the intercalary days'; IV.8: 'he takes the allotment of years and converts it to 360 days'

zr_year_365_25_days_v1.basis: the same periods measured in Julian years of 365 1/4 days: a single-setting alternative in some modern software (Stellium's documented year_length=365.25 'civil-year variant'; AstroApp's 'Year' setting), never shown beside the 360-day dates there; Valens uses 365 1/4 only for the universal year he converts from, never for the distribution
